rationale: C03 plausibly supplied material language and structure for the later telegrams. Both thank prominent associates for service, emphasize an eight-year relationship, express personal satisfaction or gratitude, praise contributions to good government or the Administration, and close with personal regard. That unusually concentrated combination is stronger than generic congratulatory language in C05 or C23.

shared_material.child_excerpt: It has been a matter of deep personal satisfaction to have served closely with you these past eight years
shared_material.parent_excerpt: your counsel during the years I have occupied the Presidency has been a source of steady satisfaction to me personally
shared_material.explanation: Both frame a long presidential association as a source of personal satisfaction.

shared_material.child_excerpt: your spirited and sustained work in the cause of good government
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Your contribution to the cause of good government will be self-evident.
shared_material.explanation: The distinctive phrase “cause of good government” is reused in praising the recipient's contribution.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I shall be forever grateful for your effective service to my Administration and the country during these past eight years.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Your work and concrete suggestions on government organization have been of substantial help... since 1953
shared_material.explanation: Both letters commend service spanning essentially the full eight years of the Eisenhower administration and its benefit to government.
